concepts.title: Growth, Its Phases and Growth Rate
concepts.definition: Growth is an irreversible permanent increase in size of an organ or its parts, measured by increase in cell number, area, weight or volume; it follows a lag phase, log phase and stationary phase, and its rate can be arithmetic or geometric and is expressed as increased growth per unit time.
concepts.key_idea: An embryo with two leaves producing twenty leaves by geometric growth doubles at each step, showing that geometric growth follows compound interest while arithmetic growth adds a constant number of cells.
question_patterns: define growth and state how it is measured in plants
describe the phases of sigmoid growth curve
differentiate arithmetic and geometric growth
calculate the percent growth rate from the given increase and initial size
what is the grand period of growth or log phase
express arithmetic growth in the form of an equation

solution_steps.action: take the increase over the initial
solution_steps.explain: Divide the increase in size by the initial size and multiply by 100 to get the percent growth rate

concepts.title: Differentiation, Dedifferentiation and Redifferentiation; Development
concepts.definition: Cells derived from meristems undergo differentiation into specialised cells, dedifferentiation regains division capacity forming interfascicular cambium, and redifferentiation matures them again; development of the plant also shows plasticity such as heterophylly and is followed by senescence and death.
concepts.key_idea: Heterophylly in cotton and coriander shows plasticity, where leaves of juvenile and mature plants take different shapes in response to environment or phases of life.
question_patterns: define differentiation dedifferentiation and redifferentiation

solution_steps.explain: Follow the cell from meristem to mature tissue and back to division.

Relate the stages to overall development and ageing.

concepts.title: Plant Growth Regulators: Auxins, Gibberellins, Cytokinins, Ethylene and ABA
concepts.definition: Plant growth regulators include auxins promoting apical dominance and rooting, gibberellins causing bolting and internode elongation, cytokinins promoting cell division and delaying senescence, gaseous ethylene promoting fruit ripening and triple response, and abscisic acid as the stress hormone closing stomata.
concepts.key_idea: Auxin's apical dominance and cytokinin's promotion of lateral buds act in opposition, and ethylene is unique among PGRs in being a gas that hastens ripening.

concepts.title: Photoperiodism and Vernalisation
concepts.definition: Photoperiodism is the response of plants to the relative length of light and dark periods, classifying them into long day, short day and day neutral plants, while vernalisation is the induction of flowering by prolonged cold treatment as in winter varieties of wheat and barley.
concepts.key_idea: The site of photoperiodic perception is the leaf, and vernalisation prevents precocious reproductive development late in the season, with the hormone behind it named vernalin.

solution_steps.explain: Check the critical photoperiod for flowering.
